newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha eases, physical trades low.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha eases, physical trades low.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices were weaker on Thursday and traders said that while large unsold north African cargoes were scarce in the prompt period, plentiful smaller pieces were available locally and out of Russia.
February swaps were talked at $224/$225 cif NWE but these remained far above the level of recent physical trade.

An end user bought a 10,000 tonne cargo of Russian Dow-quality naphtha on Wednesday at $219 cif ARA. The delivery period was between February 18 and 28. This prompt timing period underlined the discrepancy between swaps and physical markets, traders said.

Larger unsold physical cargoes were scarce but one ARA end user said he saw 45,000 tonnes of Russian naphtha available for delivery by the end of the month, as well as a 20,000 tonne piece out of northern France.
Small parcels of LVN were also seen available.

Dealers said the still high levels of swaps prices were the result of the trading strategies of a few individual players in the market, and end users said they saw the product overvalued against crude oil.
